title: 157. Byzantium and the Ghosts of Rome

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余韵》。

sentences.en: In the year 629 AD, the Roman Emperor Heraclius restored the true cross to Jerusalem in one of the greatest ceremonies in the history of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 公元629年，罗马皇帝希拉克略将真十字架送回耶路撒冷，这是罗马帝国历史上最盛大的仪式之一。

sentences.en: Heraclius, having defeated the Persians, now took for himself the title King of Kings.
sentences.zh: 希拉克略在击败波斯人后，为自己加冕了“万王之王”的头衔。

sentences.en: He also gave himself the Greek word basileus, which means sovereign or king.
sentences.zh: 他还采用了希腊语词汇“巴西琉斯”（basileus），意为君主或国王。

sentences.en: In some ways, Rome seemed to have never glittered so brightly.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上看，罗马似乎从未如此光辉灿烂过。

sentences.en: But Tom Holland, you could say that this is pretty much the moment when the Roman Empire is going to end.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆·霍兰，你可能会说，这几乎就是罗马帝国即将终结的时刻。

sentences.en: Because last time on The Rest is History, we started talking about when the Roman Empire ended.
sentences.zh: 因为在上一期《历史的余韵》中，我们开始探讨罗马帝国何时终结。

sentences.en: And you could say, couldn't you, that Heraclius is the last Roman
